lines.text: The scope of accessibility related attributes
A scope of accessibility attributes to enrich how assistive technologies
will describe text.
A list of all attribute keys contained within this scope and any sub-scopes.
The level of this heading.
Custom, localized text attributes.
The textual context.
Customizes whether punctuation should be spoken.
Customizes the pitch the spoken speech.
Customizes whether each character should be spoken separately.
Customizes if speech announcements should be queued.
The International Phonetic Alphabet representation for speech.
Customizes whether speech announcements should be queued or interrupted.
An attribute for the level of this heading.
Assistive technologies can use this property to improve
navigation and describe the level number of levels
``HeadingLevel/h1`` through ``HeadingLevel/h6``
alongside the text.
For example, you can rank sections within UI using a heading level.
The most important section is marked with``HeadingLevel/h1``.
Nested sections can use subsequent heading levels. For unranked
headings, use ``HeadingLevel/unspecified``.
The hierarchy of a heading in relation other headings.
Assistive technologies can use this to improve a users navigation
through multiple headings. When users navigate through top level
headings they expect the content for each heading to be unrelated.

is `Int`.
This function throws an error if any values are invalid for the given

- Parameter encoder: The encoder to write data to.
Creates a new instance by decoding from the given decoder, when the
type's `RawValue` is `Int`.
This initializer throws an error if reading from the decoder fails, or

- Parameter decoder: The decoder to read data from.
Returns a Boolean value indicating whether two values are not equal.
Inequality is the inverse of equality. For any values `a` and `b`, `a != b`
implies that `a == b` is `false`.
This is the default implementation of the not-equal-to operator (`!=`)
for any type that conforms to `Equatable`.
- Parameters:
- lhs: A value to compare.
- rhs: Another value to compare.
Creates a new instance with the specified raw value.
If there is no value of the type that corresponds with the specified raw
value, this initializer returns `nil`. For example:
enum PaperSize: String {
case A4, A5, Letter, Legal
print(PaperSize(rawValue: "Legal"))
// Prints "Optional(PaperSize.Legal)"
print(PaperSize(rawValue: "Tabloid"))
// Prints "nil"
- Parameter rawValue: The raw value to use for the new instance.
The raw type that can be used to represent all values of the conforming
type.
Every distinct value of the conforming type has a corresponding unique
value of the `RawValue` type, but there may be values of the `RawValue`
type that don't have a corresponding value of the conforming type.
The corresponding value of the raw type.
A new instance initialized with `rawValue` will be equivalent to this
instance. For example:
enum PaperSize: String {
case A4, A5, Letter, Legal
let selectedSize = PaperSize.Letter
print(selectedSize.rawValue)
// Prints "Letter"
print(selectedSize == PaperSize(rawValue: selectedSize.rawValue)!)
// Prints "true"
An attribute for custom, localized text attributes.
Assistive technologies can describe these attributes
alongside the text.
An attribute for the textual context.
Assistive technologies can use this property to choose
an appropriate way to output the text. For example, when
encountering a source coding context, VoiceOver could
choose to speak all punctuation.
- Note: This attribute is not used on macOS

presentation of spoken text.

An attribute to define how punctuation should be spoken.
When `true`, all punctuation will be spoken. When
`false`, no punctuation will be spoken. If this attribute
is not present, the user's settings will be used.
An attribute to adjust the pitch the spoken speech.
Values between `-1` and `0` result in a lower pitch while
values between `0` and `1` result in a higher pitch.
For example, you may want to lower the pitch when
an object is deleted, or raise the pitch if an object is inserted.
An attribute to define if each character should be spoken separately.
For example, a number representing a series of digits, like 25,
spoken as "two-five" rather than "twenty-five". Another usecase
is acronyms, like APPL, spoken as "A-P-P-L"
An attribute to define if speech announcements spoken
by VoiceOver should be queued behind existing speech
rather than interrupting speech in progress.
When `true`, the announcement will be queued behind
existing speech. When `false`, it will interrupt existing speech.
By default, announcements interrupt existing speech.
- Note: This attribute is not used on macOS
An attribute to define the International Phonetic Alphabet
representation for speech.
The IPA representation defines pronunciation of words that
have the same spelling but different sounds.
For example, consider the different pronunciations of the word
"live" in the following two sentences:
- "Anne wants to live on Main Street."
- "Maria wants to go to the live concert."
In the first sentence, “live” rhymes with "give."  Its IPA representation
would be “lɪv”. In the second sentence, it rhymes with "hive". Its
IPA representation would be “laɪv”.
- Note: This attribute is not used on macOS
An attribute to define the urgency of the announcement.
For example, when `low` is specified, announcements are queued
and spoken when other speech utterances have completed. When
`default` is specified, announcements will interrupt existing speech,
but are interruptible if a new speech utterance is started. When `high`
is specified, announcements will interrupt other speech and cannot be
interrupted once started.
A priority level used by accessibility clients, such as VoiceOver, to
control how announcements are queued and presented.
